text:
mika: FYI ran overnight kv-cache stress on magnet16k-int4 and saw divergence vs fp32 baseline after ~9k tokens. outputs drifted, seems RoPE phase has a step at a boundary. attaching minimal sample in a follow-up.

deepa: yikes. did you try zeroing rotary_scale or using the old multiplier? :thinking_face:

mika: tried rotary_scale=true/false. with scale=0.9 amplitude of phase shift drops but divergence still happens. quant config below:
```
model: magnet16k-int4
quant: int4-neg4-hybrid
prefill: enabled
rotary_scale: 0.9
kv_stride: 128
```

josh: which runtime/build? and can you paste a tiny repro prompt and the two outputs?

mika: runtime v1.12-rc3 on dedicated-dev. repro prompt is simple: 'A'*9200 + '\nQ: what are the last 3 tokens?'
FP32 baseline returns: '... tokenX tokenY tokenZ'
INT4 returns: '... tokenX tokenY tokenW' (Z->W mismatch).

deepa: hm could be KV-index wrap or shard boundary off-by-one around 8192. did you check the prefill->inflight handoff code?

mika: yes, traced the handoff traces. rope_phase value (float) jumps right at token 8192 in the trace, then downstream attention lookup uses shifted indices. prepended trace snippet shows phase before/after boundary.

sam: quick suggestion: run with `--kv-debug=indices,phase` and also try prefill stride=64/256 to see sensitivity. grep for duplicated indices.

mika: I already tried stride=64/256. stride=128 reduces divergence amplitude but doesn't eliminate it. running `--kv-debug=indices,phase` now; job started, ETA ~12m. will drop logs in this thread.

triage-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-789 | kv-cache-rope-phase-drift | assignees: mika, deepa

josh: when you paste logs, include the exact index sequences around the boundary and the rotary_phase floats (3 decimal places). makes it easier to diff.

mika: ack. uploading logs in 10m. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
